body:
# Nǚwā, spelled the way the sources wrote it
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *nuwa*. This is the file on how **Nǚwā** replaced it.

Nǚwā's two great myths answer the two great questions: where people came from, and why the sky holds. Both are told in the earliest strata of Chinese myth and never improved upon. The Huáinánzǐ tells it: in high antiquity the four pillars snapped, the nine provinces split; fire raged unquenched, waters rose undrained; fierce beasts devoured the people.  Nǚwā melted stones of five colors to mend the azure sky, cut the legs of the great turtle to set the four pillars, slew the black dragon to save Jì province, and heaped reed-ashes to dam the flood.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Nǚwā
- **ASCII form:** nuwa
- **Meaning:** "Woman wa"
- **Domain of influence:** Creation, Mending Heaven
- **Pantheon:** Chinese
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 女媧
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 168 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **女媧**. On the evidence, it means "Woman wa".

Strip **Nǚwā** to *nuwa* and 2 pieces of evidence vanish:

- **u → ǚ** — Stress on u: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.
- **a → ā** — Long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Nǚwā** lives at [/sites/nuwa/](/sites/nuwa/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/nuwa/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/nuwa/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/nuwa/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Nǚwā** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Disaster Resilience & Recovery** — The five-colored stones; catastrophe answered with repair.
- **Forestry, Conservation & Outdoor Industries** — The mender of the broken sky; restoration as divinity.
- **Environmental & Climate Services** — Reed ashes against the flood; the first climate repair.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Chinese tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Tao Te Ching](/texts/tao-te-ching/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
